First, try to drink more water. Many people drink coffee or soda all day and forget about water. A big glass of water in the morning is a good start. Second, walk more. You can get off the bus one stop early or take the stairs instead of the elevator.

Sleep is also very important. Adults need seven to nine hours of sleep every night. If you go to bed at the same time every day, it is easier to fall asleep. It is also a good idea to put your phone away an hour before bed.
Finally, eat more fruit and vegetables. They are cheaper than many people think, and they make you feel better. Healthy habits take time, but they are worth it.

title: My Hometown
paragraphs: I grew up in a small town by the sea. About five thousand people live there. When I was a child, I thought it was the most boring place in the world. Now I think it is one of the most beautiful.

The town has one main street with a few shops, two cafes, and a post office. At the end of the street, there is a long beach with white sand. In summer, the town is full of tourists, and it is noisy and busy. In winter, it is very quiet, and the wind is cold.
My parents still live there, in the same house. I visit them three or four times a year. When I arrive, I always walk on the beach first. The smell of the sea makes me feel like a child again.
I live in a big city now, and I like my life here. But my small town will always be home.

title: The Best Vacation Ever
paragraphs: Three years ago, I went to Italy with my sister. It was our first trip abroad together, and it was the best vacation of my life. We spent two weeks there and visited four cities.

We started in Rome. We saw the famous old buildings and threw coins into a fountain. Then we took a train to Florence, where we visited museums and ate the best ice cream I have ever tasted. After that, we went to Venice. There are no cars there, only boats, and the streets are full of water.

Our last stop was a small village by the sea. We stayed with a family, and the grandmother cooked dinner for us every night. She didn't speak English, and we didn't speak Italian, but we laughed a lot.
When we came home, we were sad. Now we are saving money, because next year we want to go to Spain.

title: A Day in the Life of a Nurse
paragraphs: Maria works as a nurse in a children's hospital. Her day usually starts at seven in the morning, but she gets up at half past five. She takes a bus and a train to get to work.

When she arrives, she talks to the night nurses. They tell her about the children and any problems during the night. Then she visits every child on her floor. She checks their temperature, gives them medicine, and talks to their parents.

Some days are very difficult. Some children are very sick, and their parents are worried and scared. Maria tries to be calm and kind. She often plays games with the children or reads them stories, because it helps them forget the hospital for a while.
Maria finishes work at seven in the evening. She is always tired, but she says her job is the most important thing in her life. She can't imagine doing anything else.

title: Shopping Online
paragraphs: Ten years ago, most people went to shops to buy clothes, books, and electronics. Today, many people buy almost everything online. You can order food, furniture, and even a car from your sofa.

Online shopping has many advantages. It is fast and easy, and you can do it at any time of the day or night. You can compare prices from many shops in a few minutes. Things are often cheaper online, and they come to your door.

But there are some problems too. You can't touch or try on the things before you buy them. Sometimes clothes are the wrong size, and you have to send them back. Some people also miss the experience of walking around a market or a bookstore and talking to people.
My grandmother still prefers real shops. She says, "I want to see the tomatoes before I buy them." I think she has a good point.

title: Learning to Cook
paragraphs: When I moved into my first apartment, I couldn't cook at all. For the first month, I ate pizza, sandwiches, and instant noodles every day. I felt tired all the time, and I spent too much money.

So I decided to learn. I called my mother, and she gave me some easy recipes. I started with simple things, like scrambled eggs and pasta with tomato sauce. Then I tried soup and rice dishes. Some of my first meals were terrible. Once, I burned the rice so badly that the whole apartment smelled for three days.
Slowly, I got better. I watched cooking videos and bought a good knife. I learned to use fresh vegetables and herbs. Now I cook dinner almost every evening, and I often invite friends.
Cooking is now one of my favorite hobbies. It helps me relax after work, and it is much healthier than fast food.

title: The Wrong Train
paragraphs: Last summer, Emma was traveling alone for the first time. She wanted to visit her aunt in a city about two hours away. She was nervous, but she had her ticket and a map.

At the station, it was very busy. She saw a train on platform four and got on quickly. She found a seat by the window and started to read her book. After an hour, she looked out of the window. There were fields and cows, but no city. Something was wrong.
Emma asked the woman next to her. "This train goes to the coast," the woman said. Emma's face went red. She was on the wrong train! At the next station, she got off and called her aunt.
Her aunt laughed. "Don't worry," she said. "I'll come and get you." The next day, they went to the coast together, because Emma said it looked beautiful from the train.

title: My Grandfather's Stories
paragraphs: My grandfather was born in a small village eighty years ago. His family was poor, and he started working on a farm when he was only twelve years old. He didn't go to school for very long, but he was very clever.

When I was a child, I spent every summer at his house. In the evenings, we sat outside and he told me stories about his life. He told me about the cold winters, when the snow was higher than the windows. He told me about the day he met my grandmother at a dance.

My favorite story was about his first trip to the city. He was nineteen, and he had never seen a tall building or a bus before. He got lost and walked around for hours until a police officer helped him.
My grandfather died two years ago. I miss him a lot, but I still remember all his stories, and now I tell them to my children.

title: Watching the Weather
paragraphs: Every evening, my father watches the weather forecast on television. He says it is the most important part of the news. He is a farmer, so the weather is very important for his work.

When the forecast says it will rain, he is happy in spring, because the plants need water. But in late summer, rain can be a problem, because it is time to collect the wheat. If it rains too much, the wheat gets wet and bad.

Weather forecasts are much better than they were in the past. Scientists use satellites and powerful computers to predict the weather. Today, a forecast for the next three days is usually correct. But a forecast for two weeks is still a guess.
My father doesn't always trust the television. He also looks at the sky, the clouds, and the birds. He says the birds fly lower before it rains. Sometimes he is right, and the television is wrong.

title: Learning a New Language
paragraphs: Last year, I started to learn Spanish. I wanted to travel to South America, and I wanted to talk to people there. I joined an evening class at a language school near my office.

At first, it was very difficult. The grammar was confusing, and I couldn't remember new words. In the first lesson, the teacher spoke only Spanish, and I understood almost nothing. I felt stupid and wanted to give up.

But I didn't. I studied for twenty minutes every day. I used an app on my phone, and I watched Spanish movies with subtitles. I also found a conversation partner online. Her name is Lucia, and she lives in Mexico. Every Sunday, we talk for an hour, half in Spanish and half in English.
Now, after one year, I can have simple conversations. I still make a lot of mistakes, but I am not afraid to speak. Next summer, I am going to Peru.

title: The School Trip
paragraphs: In May, our class went on a school trip to the capital city. We traveled by bus, and the trip took five hours. Everybody was excited, and nobody slept on the bus.

On the first day, we visited the national museum. We saw old paintings, ancient coins, and the clothes of kings and queens. Our guide was very funny, and she told us strange stories about the past. In the evening, we stayed in a youth hostel. I shared a room with three friends, and we talked until two in the morning.
The next day, we went on a boat trip on the river and saw the most famous buildings in the city. Then we had free time for shopping. I bought some postcards and a small present for my mother.
We came home on the third day. We were tired, but it was the best school trip ever. I took more than two hundred photos.

title: The Dog at the Door
paragraphs: One rainy night in November, my family heard a noise at the front door. My father opened it, and there was a small brown dog. It was wet, thin, and very scared. It didn't have a collar.

We brought the dog inside and gave it some food and water. It ate everything very quickly. Then it lay down in front of the heater and slept. My little brother wanted to keep it, but my mother said, "Maybe it has a family. We have to look for them."
The next day, we took the dog to the vet. The vet checked it, but there was no chip. We put posters on the trees in our street and wrote a message online. Nobody called.
After two weeks, my mother said, "OK, the dog can stay." My brother was so happy that he jumped up and down. We called the dog Lucky, because it was lucky to find us. Now Lucky is part of our family.

title: Moving to a New City
paragraphs: Six months ago, I moved to a new city for work. I didn't know anybody here, and the first weeks were very lonely. I went to work, came home, and watched television. On the weekends, I didn't talk to anybody.

Then I decided to change things. I joined a running club that meets in the park on Tuesday evenings. The people were very friendly, and after the run, we often went to a cafe. I also started a pottery class on Saturdays.
Slowly, I made some friends. Now I have a group of people I see every week. Last month, one of them invited me to her birthday party, and I met even more people there.

Moving to a new place is hard, especially when you are alone. My advice is to say yes to everything. Go to every party, join a club, and talk to your neighbors. It is scary at first, but it really helps.

title: Pancakes on Sunday
paragraphs: In my family, Sunday breakfast is always pancakes. My father started this tradition when I was a little girl, and we still do it today. Even now, when I visit my parents, we make pancakes together.

The recipe is very simple. You need flour, milk, eggs, a little sugar, and a little salt. You mix everything in a big bowl until it is smooth. Then you heat a pan with a little butter and pour in some of the mixture. When you see small bubbles on top, you turn the pancake over.
The first pancake is never perfect. My father always says, "The first one is for the cook," and he eats it himself. The rest are golden and soft.
We eat them with different things. My mother likes lemon and sugar. My brother puts chocolate on everything. I prefer fresh berries and honey. It is a simple meal, but it is full of happy memories.

title: Marie Curie
paragraphs: Marie Curie was one of the most famous scientists in history. She was born in Poland in eighteen sixty-seven. At that time, women could not study at the university in Poland, so she moved to Paris when she was twenty-four.

In Paris, she studied physics and mathematics. She was very poor, and her small room was very cold in winter. Sometimes she forgot to eat because she was studying. She met another scientist, Pierre Curie, and they got married.

Together, Marie and Pierre studied radioactivity. They discovered two new elements. In nineteen oh three, they won the Nobel Prize in Physics. Marie was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize. Later, she won a second Nobel Prize, in chemistry.
Marie Curie worked very hard all her life. Her work helped doctors and scientists, and it is still important today. She showed the world that women can be great scientists.

title: The Surprise Party
paragraphs: Last Friday was my best friend Jake's thirtieth birthday. His wife, Anna, wanted to have a surprise party for him. She invited twenty people and asked me to help.
The plan was simple. I had to take Jake to the movies in the evening. Meanwhile, Anna and the guests decorated the apartment and prepared the food. At nine o'clock, I had to bring Jake back home.
But there was a problem. In the middle of the movie, Jake said, "I'm tired. Let's go home." I didn't know what to do. I told him I wanted to see the end, but he didn't want to stay. So we left early.

I sent Anna a quick message from the car. When we got to the apartment, everything was dark and quiet. Jake opened the door, and everybody shouted, "Surprise!" Jake was so shocked that he dropped his keys. Then he laughed and said, "I knew something was strange about you tonight."

title: Why I Love the Library
paragraphs: When I was a child, my mother took me to the public library every Saturday. I could borrow five books each week. I read all of them before the next Saturday. The library was my favorite place in the world.

Today, I still go to the library, but for different reasons. Of course, I still borrow books. But the library also has free internet, newspapers from many countries, and quiet rooms where I can work. When my apartment is too noisy, I go there to concentrate.

Libraries also offer many free activities. My local library has a book club, English classes for new immigrants, and computer lessons for older people. On Saturday mornings, there is a story hour for small children.

Some people think libraries are not necessary anymore, because everything is on the internet. I don't agree. A library is a place for everybody, rich or poor, young or old. It is free, warm, and open to all.

title: The Old Bookstore
paragraphs: On a narrow street in the old part of town, there is a small bookstore. It is more than a hundred years old, and it belongs to an old man called Mr. Gray. His father and his grandfather owned it before him.

The store is dark and a little dusty. There are books everywhere, on the shelves, on the tables, and even on the floor. Some books are new, but most of them are old and secondhand. There is a strange, sweet smell of old paper. There is no music and no coffee machine, only a big gray cat who sleeps in the window.

Mr. Gray knows every book in the store. If you tell him what you like, he will always find something perfect for you. Last winter, he gave me an old book of poems. "You will love this," he said. He was right.
Many small bookstores closed in the last twenty years, because people buy books online. But Mr. Gray's store is still open. He says that people need a place where they can get lost in books.

title: Riding to Work
paragraphs: Last spring, I decided to ride my bike to work instead of driving. My office is eight kilometers from my home. At first, my friends thought I was crazy. "What about the rain?" they asked. "What about the hills?"

The first week was hard. My legs hurt, and I arrived at work hot and tired. I had to take a change of clothes in my bag. But after two weeks, it got easier. After a month, I didn't want to drive anymore.

Riding to work has changed my life. I feel healthier and stronger, and I sleep better at night. I save a lot of money on gas and parking. And I am never stuck in traffic. In the morning, I ride through the park, and I see the sun come up over the lake. It is the best part of my day.
Of course, I don't ride in heavy snow or storms. On those days, I take the bus. But I ride almost every day, and I am much happier.

title: The Talent Show
paragraphs: Every year, Mia's school had a talent show. Students sang, danced, played music, and told jokes. Mia loved watching it, but she was too shy to be in it. She could play the violin very well, but she only played at home.

This year, her music teacher said, "Mia, you have to play in the show. You are really good." Mia said no at first. But her teacher didn't stop asking, and finally Mia agreed. For three weeks, she practiced every day after school.
On the night of the show, the hall was full. Mia's hands were cold, and her heart was beating fast. When she walked onto the stage, she saw hundreds of faces. She closed her eyes and started to play.

When she finished, the hall was silent for a second. Then everybody stood up and clapped. Mia opened her eyes and saw her parents. Her mother was crying. Mia didn't win the competition, but she didn't care. She wasn't shy anymore.

title: Food Around the World
paragraphs: When people travel, they often try new and unusual food. Some of it is delicious, and some of it is very strange. Every country has its own special dishes.

In Japan, people eat a lot of raw fish. Sushi is rice with raw fish or vegetables, and it is now popular all over the world. In Mexico, people often eat tacos. These are soft corn tortillas with meat, beans, cheese, and spicy sauce. In India, many families eat rice and curry every day. Indian food uses many spices, like ginger, garlic, and cumin.

Some dishes surprise visitors. In some countries, people eat insects, like crickets and ants. They are full of protein, and some people say they taste like nuts. In Scotland, people eat haggis, which is made from the heart and other parts of a sheep.
I always try the local food when I travel. Sometimes I don't like it, but it is always interesting. Food tells you a lot about a culture.

title: The First Snow
paragraphs: I grew up in a hot country, and I didn't see snow until I was twenty-five. That year, I moved to Canada to study at a university. I arrived in September, when the weather was still warm and sunny.
In November, the weather changed. It got colder every week, and the days got shorter. My friends told me to buy a big winter coat and good boots. I didn't believe them. "How cold can it be?" I said.

One morning in December, I woke up and the room was very bright. I looked out of the window, and everything was white. The trees, the cars, and the streets were all covered in snow. I ran outside in my pajamas and touched it. It was so cold and soft. I laughed like a child.
That winter was very hard for me. Sometimes it was minus twenty-five degrees. But I will never forget that first morning of snow.

title: My Sister, the Doctor
paragraphs: My older sister, Hannah, always wanted to be a doctor. When she was a little girl, she played doctor with her dolls. She put bandages on them and gave them pretend medicine.

At school, she was always the best student in her class. She studied very hard, especially science. After high school, she went to medical school. It took her many years, and it was very difficult. She often studied until two or three in the morning, and she didn't have much free time.

Now Hannah is thirty-two, and she works in a big hospital in the city. She is a children's doctor. She works long hours, and sometimes she works at night or on the weekend. When she comes to our parents' house for dinner, she often falls asleep on the sofa.
I am very proud of my sister. She is smart, kind, and very hardworking. She says the best part of her job is when a sick child gets better and goes home.

title: The Farmers' Market
paragraphs: Every Saturday morning, there is a farmers' market in the main square of our town. Farmers from the villages around the town bring their fruit, vegetables, cheese, eggs, and bread. The market starts at seven o'clock and finishes at one.

I always go early, at about eight, because the best things sell quickly. I take two big bags and walk around slowly. I like to talk to the farmers. They tell me which vegetables are the freshest and how to cook them.

The food at the market is a little more expensive than in the supermarket. But it is fresher, and it tastes much better. The tomatoes taste like real tomatoes, and the strawberries are sweet and juicy. I also like knowing where my food comes from.
After shopping, I usually have a coffee at a small cafe next to the square. I sit outside and watch the people. For me, it is the perfect way to start the weekend.

title: The Big Storm
paragraphs: Last October, there was a big storm in our town. The weather forecast said it was going to be bad, so most people stayed at home. The schools closed, and many shops didn't open.

The storm started in the afternoon. First, the wind got stronger and stronger. Then the rain came. It was so heavy that I couldn't see the houses across the street. At about six o'clock, the electricity went off. We lit candles and sat together in the living room. My little sister was scared, so my father told funny stories.

The wind was very loud all night. We heard a crash in the garden, but we didn't go outside. In the morning, the storm was over. A big tree was lying across our garden. It broke the fence, but luckily it didn't hit the house.
All the neighbors came out to help each other. We cleaned the streets together. It was a terrible storm, but it brought our street closer together.

title: The Language Exchange
paragraphs: Last year, I wanted to improve my French, but I didn't have money for lessons. Then a friend told me about a language exchange. In a language exchange, two people help each other learn their languages for free.

I found a partner on a website. His name was Lucas, and he was a student from Lyon. He wanted to practice his English. We decided to meet online every Thursday evening. For thirty minutes we spoke French, and then for thirty minutes we spoke English.

At first, I was nervous, and I made a lot of mistakes. But Lucas was very patient. He corrected me in a friendly way, and he taught me words that young people really use. I helped him with his pronunciation, because he found English sounds very difficult.
After six months, my French was much better. Last summer, I visited Lyon, and Lucas showed me his city. Now we are good friends, and we still talk every week.

title: The Baby Bird
paragraphs: One morning in May, Sam was walking to school when he heard a small sound under a tree. He looked down and saw a tiny bird on the grass. It didn't have many feathers, and it couldn't fly. It was crying for its mother.

Sam looked up into the tree. There was a nest on a high branch, but it was too high for him. He didn't want to leave the bird alone, because there were many cats on his street. So he carefully picked it up and put it in his hat.
He was late for school, and his teacher was not happy. But when Sam showed her the bird, she smiled. She called a man who helped injured animals. He came to the school at lunchtime and took the bird.
Three weeks later, the man sent a photo to the school. The bird was big and healthy, and it was flying. The whole class cheered. Sam kept the photo on his bedroom wall for many years.

title: A Day Without My Phone
paragraphs: Last Sunday, I tried an experiment. I turned off my phone and put it in a drawer for the whole day. I wanted to see what my life was like without it. I was a little nervous, because I use my phone for almost everything.

In the morning, I felt strange. I usually check the news and my messages in bed. Instead, I got up and made breakfast. I read a magazine while I ate. Then I went for a walk in the park. Without my phone, I noticed many things: the birds, the trees, and the people around me.
In the afternoon, I wanted to meet a friend, but I couldn't call her. So I walked to her house and knocked on the door. She was very surprised, but happy. We had coffee and talked for two hours.
In the evening, I turned my phone on again. I had forty messages, but none of them were important. I decided to do this every Sunday.

title: My Cousin's Wedding
paragraphs: Last summer, my cousin Laura got married. The wedding was in a small village in the countryside, where her husband's family lives. More than a hundred and fifty people came, from five different countries.

The ceremony was in an old stone church at two o'clock. Laura wore a long white dress, and she looked beautiful. Her husband, Marco, was so nervous that he forgot some of his words. Everybody laughed, and then he laughed too.

After the ceremony, we went to a big garden for the party. There were long tables under the trees, with flowers and candles. We ate for hours. There was soup, fish, meat, salads, and a huge wedding cake with five layers. Then a band played music, and everybody danced until two in the morning. Even my grandmother danced.
It was a long day, but it was wonderful. I took a lot of photos. My favorite one shows Laura and Marco laughing in the garden.

title: Joining a Gym
paragraphs: In January, I decided to get fit. Like many people, I made a New Year's resolution. I joined a gym near my office and paid for a whole year. I was very excited.

For the first two weeks, I went every day. I ran on the machines, lifted weights, and took a yoga class. My whole body hurt, but I felt great. Then work got busy, and I started to miss days. By March, I only went once a week. By May, I didn't go at all.

I felt bad about the money, so in June I tried again. This time, I made a different plan. I found a friend who wanted to go to the gym too. We decided to meet there every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at seven in the morning.
It worked. When you have a partner, it is harder to stay at home. Now, a year later, we still go three times a week. I am stronger, and I have more energy.

title: The Science Museum
paragraphs: Last weekend, I took my two children to the science museum in the city. I wasn't sure they would like it, but it was a great day for all of us.

The museum is very different from a normal museum. You can touch almost everything. In the first room, my son made electricity with a bicycle. My daughter put her hand on a special ball, and her hair stood up. They both laughed a lot.

Upstairs, there was a big room about space. We saw a real rock from the moon and a model of a space station. We sat in a dark room and watched a film about the stars and the planets. My daughter said she wants to be an astronaut.

We stayed for five hours, and we didn't see everything. The children were tired but very happy. In the car, they asked me hundreds of questions. I couldn't answer all of them, so we are going to go back next month.

title: The Cooking Class
paragraphs: For my birthday, my husband gave me a cooking class. It was a Thai cooking class at a small restaurant in the city. There were eight students, and our teacher was the chef, a woman from Bangkok called Nok.

First, Nok showed us the ingredients. Some of them were new for me, like lemongrass and fish sauce. She explained how to choose fresh herbs and how to use them. Then we went into the kitchen, and each student had a small cooking station.

We made three dishes: a spicy soup, a green curry, and a noodle dish. Nok walked around and helped everybody. My curry was too spicy at first, so she showed me how to fix it with a little coconut milk. Everything smelled wonderful.
At the end, we sat at a long table and ate our food together. It was delicious. Now I cook Thai food at home every week, and my husband is very happy with his present.

title: An Unusual Pet
paragraphs: Most people have a cat or a dog. My friend Oliver has a snake. Her name is Bella, and she is about one and a half meters long. She lives in a big glass box in his living room.

When people visit Oliver, they are often scared of Bella. But Oliver says she is very calm and gentle. She is not dangerous, and she doesn't bite. She moves slowly, and she likes to sleep under a warm lamp. She eats only once every week or two.

Oliver says a snake is an easy pet. It doesn't make noise, it doesn't need walks, and it doesn't smell. But it needs the right temperature and a clean home. Oliver checks the temperature in the glass box every day.
The first time I held Bella, I was very nervous. Her skin was dry and smooth, not wet like I expected. Now I am not scared anymore. I still prefer cats, but I understand why Oliver loves his snake.

title: The Summer Festival
paragraphs: Every year in August, my grandparents' village has a summer festival. It lasts for three days, and people come from all the villages around. My family goes every year, and I always look forward to it.

During the day, there are games and competitions for children and adults. There is a race in the river, a cake competition, and a big soccer game between two villages. In the main square, people sell local food, like cheese, honey, and fresh bread.

In the evening, there is music and dancing. Long tables stand in the square, and everybody eats dinner together under colored lights. Old people sing traditional songs, and young people dance until late. On the last night, there are fireworks over the lake.

The festival started more than two hundred years ago, to celebrate the end of the harvest. Today, life in the village is very different. But the festival is still the most important event of the year.

title: A Big Mistake
paragraphs: Peter was the new manager at a small company. On his first Friday, he wanted to send a friendly email to his team. He wrote, "Thank you for a great first week. Let's have lunch together on Monday. I'll pay!"
He also wanted to send a message to his wife about the weekend. He wrote, "I am so tired of this job already. I just want to go home and sleep." Then he pressed send.
Five minutes later, he looked at his screen and went white. He sent the message to his wife to his whole team, and the friendly email to his wife! He didn't know what to do.

On Monday morning, he came to the office very nervous. But when he opened the door, his team was laughing. On his desk, there was a pillow and a cup of coffee with a note: "Sleep well, boss!" Peter laughed too. That lunch was the start of a great team.

title: The City at Night
paragraphs: I work at night in a hospital, so I often travel across the city at two or three in the morning. At first, I didn't like it. Now I think the city at night is a special world.

The streets are quiet, and there are only a few cars. The tall buildings are dark, except for a few windows with lights. I sometimes wonder about the people behind those windows. Are they working, reading, or just unable to sleep like me?

At night, I see different people. There are bakers who start work at three o'clock, taxi drivers, and police officers. There are cleaners in the empty offices and young people walking home from parties. There is a small cafe near the station that is open all night. I often stop there for a coffee, and the owner knows my name.
When I finish work, the sky is turning pink, and the city is waking up. Then it is time for me to sleep.

title: The Best Teacher
paragraphs: When I was fourteen, I hated math. I didn't understand it, and my grades were very bad. I thought I was just stupid. Then, in my second year of high school, we got a new math teacher, Mr. Evans.

Mr. Evans was different from the other teachers. He never shouted, and he never made students feel bad. He explained things in many different ways until everybody understood. He used examples from real life, like sports, cooking, and money.

One day, after class, he asked me to stay. I was worried, but he only said, "You are better at math than you think. You just need more confidence." He offered to help me after school on Tuesdays. For the rest of the year, I went to his classroom every week.
At the end of the year, I got the best grade in my class. Today, I am an engineer, and I use math every day. I still think about Mr. Evans and his kind words.

title: The Night Train
paragraphs: Last year, I traveled from one side of the country to the other by night train. The trip took fourteen hours. Many people asked me, "Why don't you fly? It's much faster." But I wanted an adventure.

The train left at seven in the evening. I had a small cabin with a bed, a tiny sink, and a window. I shared it with an old woman called Edith. She was traveling to see her new grandson. She had a big bag of food, and she shared her sandwiches and cookies with me.

In the evening, we sat in the restaurant car and watched the sun go down over the fields. Then I went to bed. The train moved slowly from side to side, and the sound of the wheels was relaxing. I slept better than I do at home.
When I woke up, we were in the mountains. There was snow on the trees, and the sky was bright blue. It was the most beautiful morning I can remember.

title: Our Recycling Project
paragraphs: Last year, our class started a recycling project at school. Our teacher showed us a photo of our school's trash. Every week, we threw away more than two hundred plastic bottles and a lot of paper. Most of it went into the normal trash.

We decided to change this. First, we made colorful boxes for plastic, paper, and cans, and we put them in every classroom. Then we made posters to explain the project. Every Friday, two students checked the boxes and took them to the big recycling bins behind the school.

At first, many students forgot, and they still put everything in the normal trash. So we visited every class and talked about the project. We showed them what happens to plastic in the sea. After a month, things got much better.
At the end of the year, our school recycled four times more than before. The town newspaper wrote a story about us. We were very proud.

title: The Broken Leg
paragraphs: Last winter, I went skiing with my friends for the first time. On the first day, we took a lesson, and I learned the basics. On the second day, I felt confident, so I went down a more difficult slope. That was a big mistake.

I was going too fast, and I couldn't stop. I hit a small hill and fell. I heard a terrible sound, and then I felt a lot of pain in my leg. I couldn't stand up. My friends called for help, and two men came with a special sled and took me down the mountain.

At the hospital, the doctor said my leg was broken. I had a big white cast for six weeks. I couldn't drive, I couldn't go up the stairs easily, and I couldn't take a normal shower. Everything was difficult.
But my friends were wonderful. They brought me food and played games with me. Now my leg is fine, and next year I am going to try skiing again, but more slowly.

title: The Mystery Letter
paragraphs: One morning, Clara found a strange letter in her mailbox. There was no stamp and no name on the envelope. Inside, there was a small piece of paper with only one sentence: "Go to the old oak tree in the park at four o'clock."
Clara was curious, but also a little worried. Who wrote it? And why? She showed it to her brother, Max. "It's probably a joke," he said. But at half past three, they both walked to the park.

The old oak tree was in the middle of the park, next to the lake. There was nobody there. Then Clara saw something in a hole in the tree. It was a small box with a red ribbon. Inside, there was a key and another note: "Happy birthday, Clara. Look in the garage."
Clara ran home and opened the garage. There was a new blue bike with a big bow on it. Her parents were standing next to it, smiling. She forgot it was her birthday!

title: A Market in Morocco
paragraphs: Two years ago, I visited Marrakech, a city in Morocco. The most exciting place in the city was the big market in the old town. It is a maze of narrow streets with hundreds of small shops.

When I walked in, I didn't know where to look. There were colorful carpets, leather bags, silver lamps, and piles of spices in every color. Men were cooking meat on small grills, and the air smelled of cinnamon and smoke. People were shouting, music was playing, and motorbikes were driving through the crowds.

In the market, you don't pay the first price. You have to discuss the price with the seller. At first, I was embarrassed, but then I started to enjoy it. I bought a beautiful lamp for half the first price. The seller and I drank mint tea together and laughed.
I got lost three times, but every time, somebody helped me find my way. I will never forget that market.

title: A Letter from Grandma
paragraphs: My grandmother doesn't use email or a phone. She still writes letters by hand. Every month, I receive a long letter from her in her small, neat handwriting.

She writes about her garden, her neighbors, and her cat. She tells me about the books she is reading and the recipes she is trying. Sometimes she puts a dried flower or an old photo in the envelope. Her letters always smell a little of lavender.

At first, I answered her letters with a quick phone call. But last year, I started to write letters back. It was strange at first. I haven't written by hand for years, and my writing was messy. But I enjoy it now. When I write a letter, I think more carefully about my words.
I keep all my grandmother's letters in a wooden box. There are more than fifty now. I know that one day they will be very precious to me.

title: The Quiet Neighbor
paragraphs: For three years, I lived next to a man called Mr. Novak. He was very quiet. He said "good morning" when we met on the stairs, but nothing more. I didn't know anything about him.

Then, one evening, the electricity went off in our whole building. It was very dark, and I didn't have any candles. I knocked on Mr. Novak's door to ask for help. He opened it with a candle in his hand and invited me in.

His apartment was full of musical instruments: violins, guitars, and an old piano. He told me he was a music teacher for forty years. While we waited for the electricity, he played the piano for me by candlelight. It was beautiful.

After that night, we became friends. Every Sunday, I visited him for tea, and he told me about his life and his travels. He moved away last year to live with his daughter, but we still write to each other. I learned that quiet people often have the best stories.

title: The Final Game
paragraphs: Last season, my daughter's soccer team got to the final of the city competition. The girls were only eleven years old, but they played very well all year. Nobody expected them to get so far.

The final was on a cold Saturday morning in March. The other team was bigger and stronger, and they won the competition the year before. At half time, our team was losing two goals to zero. The girls were sad and tired, and some of them were crying.

Their coach talked to them quietly. She didn't shout. She told them she was proud of them, and that they had nothing to lose. In the second half, the girls played like a different team. They scored one goal, and then another. Two minutes before the end, my daughter scored the third goal.
The parents went crazy. We jumped, shouted, and hugged each other. The girls won three goals to two, and they lifted the cup together. I will never forget their faces.

title: Working at the Zoo
paragraphs: For two summers, when I was a university student, I worked at the city zoo. My job was to help the animal keepers. I wanted to be a vet, so it was perfect for me.

The work started at seven o'clock in the morning. First, we cleaned the animals' homes. It was dirty and smelly work, and I was always wet. Then we prepared the food. Every animal had a special diet. The monkeys ate fruit and vegetables, and the lions ate meat. The penguins ate fish, of course.

My favorite animals were the elephants. There were three of them, and each one had a different personality. The oldest one, Rosie, was very calm. She knew all the keepers, and she always touched my arm with her trunk when I said hello.
The job wasn't easy, and the money wasn't great. But I learned so much about animals. Today I am a vet, and I still visit the zoo sometimes.

title: New Year's Eve
paragraphs: In my family, New Year's Eve is the most important party of the year. Every year on December thirty-first, my whole family meets at my parents' house. There are usually about twenty people, from babies to great-grandparents.

We start cooking in the afternoon. My mother makes her famous salad, my aunt brings a big roast chicken, and my grandmother bakes three different cakes. The children decorate the house with balloons and lights. In the evening, we sit at a long table and eat for hours.

At about half past eleven, we write our wishes for the new year on small pieces of paper. We don't show them to anybody. Just before midnight, we turn on the television and count down the last ten seconds together. Then everybody hugs and kisses, and we go outside to watch the fireworks.
We usually go to bed at three or four in the morning. The next day is always very quiet.

title: A Garden on the Roof
paragraphs: I live in an apartment in the city center, and I don't have a garden. For years, I wanted to grow my own vegetables. Then, two years ago, my neighbors and I had an idea. Why not use the flat roof of our building?

We asked the building owner, and he said yes. We bought big wooden boxes and filled them with soil. In spring, we planted tomatoes, lettuce, beans, and herbs. Everybody in the building helped. Some people watered the plants, and some people pulled out the weeds.

That first summer, we had more vegetables than we could eat. We shared them with everybody in the building. We also put a table and some chairs on the roof. In the evenings, we often eat dinner there together and watch the sun go down over the city.
Before the garden, I didn't know most of my neighbors. Now they are my friends. The garden gave us more than vegetables.

title: A Photo from the Past
paragraphs: In my parents' living room, there is a black and white photo of a busy street. It shows our town about a hundred years ago. I often look at it and try to imagine life at that time.

In the photo, there are no cars. People are walking in the middle of the street, and there is a horse and cart outside a shop. The women are wearing long dresses and big hats, and the men are wearing dark suits. A group of children is playing with a ball near the church.

The church is still there today, and so are some of the buildings. But most things are very different now. The street is full of traffic, and there are big supermarkets and banks instead of small shops.
My great-grandfather is in the photo. He is the young man standing in front of the bakery. He owned that bakery for thirty years. Today, it is a phone shop.

title: My First Race
paragraphs: Two years ago, I couldn't run for more than five minutes. I was always tired, and I didn't do any exercise. Then my best friend asked me to run a ten kilometer race with her. I laughed. "Me? I can't run," I said. But she didn't give up.

We started training together in January. On the first day, we ran for one minute and walked for two minutes, ten times. It was very hard. Every week, we ran a little more and walked a little less. After two months, I could run for thirty minutes without stopping.
The race was in June. On the day, I was very nervous. There were thousands of people, music, and crowds. The first five kilometers were OK, but then it got very hot, and my legs hurt.
My friend stayed with me the whole time. When we saw the finish line, we held hands and ran together. It took us one hour and five minutes. I cried at the end. I was so proud.

title: The Strange Noise
paragraphs: For a week, Tom and his wife heard a strange noise in their house every night. It started at about midnight. It was a quiet scratching sound, and it came from the wall in the kitchen.

"It's a mouse," said Tom. They put food out, but nothing happened. The next night, the noise was louder. Tom's wife couldn't sleep. "Maybe it's a ghost," she said, only half joking. The house was very old, and some neighbors told strange stories about it.

On Saturday, Tom decided to find out. He moved the big kitchen cupboard away from the wall. Behind it, there was a small hole. He put a flashlight in the hole and looked inside. Two shining eyes looked back at him.

It wasn't a mouse or a ghost. It was a mother cat with four tiny kittens. She probably came in through a broken window in the basement. Tom and his wife kept one of the kittens. They called him Ghost.

title: A Week in New York
paragraphs: Last spring, I spent a week in New York with my best friend. It was our first time in the United States. We saved money for a long time, and we were very excited.

The city was bigger and busier than I imagined. The buildings were so tall that my neck hurt from looking up. There were people everywhere, speaking many different languages. On the first day, we walked for eight hours and saw only a small part of the city.

We did many famous things. We visited the Statue of Liberty and took the boat across the harbor. We walked across the Brooklyn Bridge at sunset. We spent a whole day in Central Park and ate hot dogs from a street cart. In the evening, we went to the top of a tall building and looked at the lights of the city.
New York was expensive, and it was very noisy. But it was exciting, and I loved it. I want to go back one day.

title: The Repair Cafe
paragraphs: Once a month, there is a repair cafe in the community center near my home. People bring broken things, and volunteers help them repair them for free. You can drink coffee and eat cake while you wait.

Last month, I took my old lamp and a jacket with a broken zipper. There were about thirty people there. A retired engineer looked at my lamp. He showed me the problem and helped me change a small part. In ten minutes, it worked again. Then a woman with a sewing machine fixed my zipper.

Many people throw things away when they break. It is often cheaper to buy something new. But this creates a lot of waste, and it is bad for the environment. At the repair cafe, people learn how to repair their things themselves.
I enjoyed the afternoon very much. I learned something new, and I met interesting people. Next month, I am going to go again. Maybe I will be a volunteer too.

title: The Birthday Cake
paragraphs: When my son was five, he asked for a special birthday cake. He wanted a cake that looked like a dinosaur. A cake like that costs a lot of money in a shop, so I decided to make it myself.

I found a recipe on the internet and bought everything I needed. On the night before the party, I started baking. I made two big chocolate cakes and let them cool. Then I tried to cut them into the shape of a dinosaur. It was much harder than it looked in the video.

My first dinosaur looked like a potato. My second dinosaur looked like a potato with legs. At two o'clock in the morning, I was tired and angry. I covered the whole cake with green icing and put some candy on it for eyes and teeth.
The next day, I was worried. But when my son saw the cake, he shouted, "A dinosaur!" and hugged me. All the children loved it. It was not perfect, but it was made with love.

title: The Tree House
paragraphs: When I was nine years old, my father built a tree house for me and my brother. It was in an old apple tree at the bottom of our garden. It took him four weekends, and we helped him carry the wood.

The tree house was small, with one window and a door. To get in, you had to climb a rope ladder. Inside, there was space for two children and a small table. We put old cushions on the floor and pictures on the walls.

That tree house became our secret place. We read comics there, ate snacks, and made plans for adventures. In summer, we sometimes slept there with our sleeping bags. We could hear the owls at night, and it was a little scary, but exciting.
Many years later, my parents sold the house. The new family has two small children. Last summer, I drove past, and I saw two little faces in the window of the tree house. It made me very happy.

title: The Chess Club
paragraphs: At my school, there is a chess club every Wednesday after lessons. I joined it last year because my friend Leo was a member. I didn't really know how to play. I only knew how the pieces moved.

The club teacher, Mrs. Patel, is a very good player. She taught us the basic rules and some simple strategies. She told us to always think before we move and to look at the whole board. In my first games, I lost very quickly, sometimes in only ten moves.

But I didn't give up. I played chess on my computer at home and read a book about famous games. Slowly, I started to win some games. Chess taught me to be patient and to think about the future, not only about the next move.
In March, our club played in a competition against other schools. I won four games and lost two. Our team came second. Now chess is my favorite hobby.

title: Life on a Small Island
paragraphs: My friend Sara lives on a very small island. Only about three hundred people live there. There are no cars on the island, only bicycles and a few small tractors. To get to the mainland, you have to take a boat. It takes forty minutes.

Life on the island is very simple. There is one shop, one school, one doctor, and one cafe. Everybody knows everybody. When somebody is sick or needs help, the neighbors are always there. Children play outside all day, because it is very safe.

But life there is not always easy. In winter, there are big storms, and sometimes the boat can't go for days. Then there is no fresh food in the shop. Many young people leave the island when they finish school, because there are not many jobs.
Sara says she would never live anywhere else. She loves the quiet, the sea, and the people. When I visit her, I understand why.

title: Helping at the Animal Shelter
paragraphs: Every Saturday morning, I work as a volunteer at an animal shelter near my town. The shelter takes care of dogs and cats that don't have a home. Some of them were lost, and some of them were left by their owners.

When I arrive, I first clean the cages and give the animals fresh water and food. Then I take the dogs for walks, two at a time. Some dogs are very excited and pull hard. Others are scared and walk slowly behind me. I always talk to them quietly.

My favorite dog was an old black dog called Shadow. He was at the shelter for almost a year, because most people want young dogs. Every week, I spent extra time with him. He loved to lie in the sun while I brushed him.
Last month, an older couple came to the shelter. They wanted a calm dog, and they chose Shadow. I was sad to say goodbye, but very happy for him. Now he has a family.

title: My First Flight
paragraphs: I didn't fly on a plane until I was thirty. I was always afraid of flying. When my company sent me to a meeting in another country, I didn't have a choice. I had to go.

The night before the flight, I couldn't sleep. At the airport, my hands were wet, and my heart was beating fast. On the plane, I sat next to a young woman with a baby. She saw I was nervous and started talking to me. She told me she flew every month for her job.

When the plane took off, I closed my eyes and held the seat very tight. The noise was very loud, and my stomach felt strange. But after a few minutes, everything was calm. I opened my eyes and looked out of the window. We were above the clouds, and the sun was shining. It was beautiful.
The flight took three hours. When we landed, I felt very proud. I still don't love flying, but now I am not afraid.

title: The Secret Recipe
paragraphs: In a small town, there was a restaurant famous for its tomato soup. People came from other cities just to try it. The owner, an old woman called Rosa, never told anybody the secret recipe.

When Rosa got older, she wanted to retire. Her grandson, Luca, wanted to take over the restaurant. "Please, Grandma," he said, "tell me the secret of your soup." Rosa smiled. "I will show you," she said. "Come to the kitchen tomorrow at six in the morning."

The next morning, Luca watched carefully. Rosa used fresh tomatoes, onions, garlic, olive oil, and a little salt. Nothing special. She cooked the soup very slowly for three hours and tasted it many times. "But what is the secret ingredient?" asked Luca.
Rosa laughed. "Time," she said. "And I make it for people I love. Everybody who comes here is family." Luca understood. Today, he runs the restaurant, and the soup is still famous.

title: Living Without a Car
paragraphs: Three years ago, my car broke down, and the repair was very expensive. I decided not to buy a new car. My friends said I was crazy, but it was one of the best decisions of my life.

At first, it was difficult. I had to plan my trips carefully. I learned the bus times, and I bought a good bicycle. For long trips, I take the train. When I really need a car, for example to move furniture, I rent one for a day.

Now I save a lot of money every month. I don't pay for gas, parking, repairs, or insurance. I also get more exercise, because I walk and ride my bike every day. I feel healthier, and I lost five kilos in the first year.

There are some disadvantages, of course. In winter, it is not fun to wait for a bus in the rain. And it is harder to visit my parents in the countryside. But for me, life without a car is simpler and calmer.

title: Lost in the Forest
paragraphs: Last autumn, my friend Kate and I went hiking in a big national park. We planned a walk of fifteen kilometers. We had a map, water, sandwiches, and warm jackets. The weather was sunny and cool.

For the first three hours, everything was perfect. We walked through forests of tall trees and saw deer and a big eagle. But in the afternoon, we took a wrong path. After an hour, we didn't recognize anything, and our phones didn't have a signal. It was starting to get dark.
We were scared, but we tried to stay calm. Kate remembered that rivers usually go down to villages. We found a small river and walked next to it. It was cold, and we were very tired and hungry.
After two more hours, we saw lights. It was a small farmhouse. A friendly farmer and his wife gave us hot tea and drove us back to our car. Now I always tell somebody my plans before I go hiking.

title: Singing Lessons
paragraphs: I always loved singing, but I only sang in the shower or in the car. I thought my voice was terrible. Then, on my fortieth birthday, my husband gave me five singing lessons as a present.

My teacher was a woman called Helen. She was about sixty, and she sang in an opera choir for many years. In the first lesson, I was so nervous that my voice was very quiet. Helen laughed kindly. "Everybody can sing," she said. "You just need to breathe."

She taught me how to stand, how to breathe from my stomach, and how to open my mouth. We practiced simple songs and exercises. Every week, my voice got a little stronger. After the five lessons, I bought ten more.
Now I sing in a choir with thirty other people. We practice every Thursday evening and give concerts at Christmas and in the summer. Singing makes me happy, and I am not afraid of my voice anymore.

title: The Old Castle
paragraphs: On a hill above my town, there is an old stone castle. It is more than eight hundred years old. Today, it is a museum, and many tourists visit it every summer.

The castle was built by a rich family to protect the town from enemies. It has thick walls, four tall towers, and a deep ditch around it. In the past, the only way in was across a wooden bridge. When enemies came, the soldiers pulled the bridge up.

Inside the castle, you can see the great hall, where the family ate big dinners, and the small rooms where they slept. In winter, it was very cold, even with big fires. There is also a dark room under the ground. It was a prison, and it is a little scary.
My favorite part is the top of the highest tower. From there, you can see the whole town, the river, and the mountains. On a clear day, you can see for more than fifty kilometers.

title: A Difficult Customer
paragraphs: Last year, I worked in a clothes shop in a shopping center. Most of the customers were nice, but one day, a woman came in who was very angry. She had a shopping bag with a dress in it.

She shouted, "This dress is terrible! I wore it once, and now there is a hole in it. I want my money back!" Everybody in the shop looked at us. I felt my face go red. I wanted to shout back, but I remembered my manager's advice: always stay calm and listen.

So I said, "I am very sorry. Can I see the dress, please?" I looked at it carefully. There was a small hole in the side. I told her I could give her a new dress or her money. Slowly, she became calmer. She chose a new dress and even said thank you.
A week later, she came back and bought three more things. She was smiling. I learned that angry people often just want somebody to listen.

title: The Photo Competition
paragraphs: Last year, my town had a photo competition. The theme was "Our Town in Winter." The prize was a new camera. I am not a professional photographer, but I love taking photos, so I decided to try.

Every weekend in December and January, I walked around the town with my old camera. I took photos of the snowy park, the frozen river, and the market with its colorful lights. I took more than five hundred photos, but most of them were not very good.
One cold morning, I saw an old man feeding birds in the park. The snow was falling, and the light was soft and golden. I took the photo quickly. When I looked at it at home, I knew it was special.

I sent that photo to the competition. A month later, I got a phone call. I won second prize! My photo was in the town newspaper and in an exhibition at the library. I didn't win the camera, but I was very happy.

title: The Lighthouse
paragraphs: On a small rock in the sea, near the coast where I grew up, there is an old white lighthouse. It is about thirty meters tall, and it was built more than a hundred and fifty years ago.

For many years, a lighthouse keeper lived there with his family. His job was to keep the light on every night, so that ships didn't hit the rocks in the dark. It was a lonely life. In bad weather, the family couldn't leave the lighthouse for weeks. The children went to school on the mainland by boat.

Today, the light is automatic, and nobody lives there. A computer turns it on and off. But in summer, small boats take tourists to visit it. You can climb the two hundred steps to the top and look at the sea.
When I was a child, I could see the light from my bedroom window. Every night, it flashed every ten seconds. It always made me feel safe.

title: Friends Forever
paragraphs: I met my best friend, Lisa, on our first day of school. We were six years old. I was crying because I missed my mother, and Lisa gave me a piece of her chocolate. From that day, we were always together.

We went to the same school for twelve years. We did our homework together, we laughed at the same jokes, and we told each other all our secrets. Sometimes we argued, but never for long. After school, Lisa went to a university in another city, and I started working. We were sad, but we called each other every week.

Now we are both thirty-five. Lisa lives in another country with her husband and her two children. We don't see each other often, maybe once a year. But when we meet, it feels like we were never apart. We talk for hours, just like when we were children.
I have many friends, but Lisa is special. She knows me better than anybody.

title: The Flood
paragraphs: Two years ago, it rained in our town for six days without stopping. The river next to the town got higher and higher. On the sixth night, the water came over the river banks and into the streets.

My family lives near the river. At three o'clock in the morning, my father woke us up. "Get up! The water is coming!" he shouted. We quickly carried important things upstairs: photos, papers, and the computer. The water came into our house and covered the whole ground floor. It was almost one meter deep.

In the morning, a boat came to take us to a school on the hill. There were many families there. People brought blankets, food, and dry clothes. Nobody was hurt, but everybody was very worried about their homes.
After a week, the water went down. Our house was dirty and wet, and we lost a lot of furniture. It took months to repair everything. But our neighbors helped us, and we helped them.

title: How Bees Talk
paragraphs: Bees are very small, but they are amazing animals. They live together in big groups called colonies. One colony can have more than fifty thousand bees. Each bee has a job, and they all work together.

Scientists discovered something surprising about bees. They can "talk" to each other with a special dance. When a bee finds a lot of flowers, it flies back to the hive. Then it dances in a special way. The dance tells the other bees where the flowers are and how far away they are.

If the flowers are close, the bee dances in a small circle. If they are far away, it dances in a line and moves its body from side to side. The direction of the dance shows the direction of the flowers. The other bees watch, and then they fly straight to the food.
Bees are very important for people too. They help many plants grow fruit and vegetables. Without bees, we would have much less food.

title: Our New Apartment
paragraphs: Last month, my boyfriend and I moved into our first apartment together. It is on the third floor of an old building in the city center. It has two bedrooms, a small kitchen, and a living room with a big window.

The apartment was not in good condition when we got it. The walls were dark and dirty, and the kitchen was very old. So we spent three weekends painting and cleaning. We painted the living room light blue and the bedroom white. My father helped us fix the kitchen door.

We didn't have much money for furniture, so we bought some things secondhand. We found a beautiful old table at a market and a comfortable sofa online. My grandmother gave us some plates and glasses. Our friends gave us plants.
Now the apartment feels like home. It is not perfect. The heating is noisy, and the shower is very small. But we love it. On Sunday mornings, we sit by the window, drink coffee, and watch the street.

title: The Red Balloon
paragraphs: At the town fair, a little girl called Amy got a big red balloon. She was very happy, and she held the string very tight. But when she was eating her ice cream, she forgot, and the balloon flew away.

Amy started to cry. The balloon went up over the trees and the houses, higher and higher, until it was only a small red dot in the sky. Her father bought her a new balloon, but she didn't want it. She wanted her red balloon.

Many kilometers away, an old farmer was working in his field. He looked up and saw something red in a tree. It was a balloon, and there was a small card on the string. On the card, it said, "My name is Amy. Please write to me." Her mother wrote the address there.
A week later, Amy got a letter with a photo of the farmer and his cows. They became pen pals, and every summer, Amy visited the farm.

title: Working from Home
paragraphs: Since last year, I work from home three days a week. On the other two days, I go to the office. At first, I loved working from home. I didn't have to take the crowded train, and I could work in comfortable clothes.

But after a few months, I noticed some problems. I started work earlier and finished later, because my office was always there, in my living room. I didn't take real breaks for lunch. And I felt lonely, because I didn't talk to my colleagues very much.

So I made some rules. I start work at nine o'clock and finish at five. I have a real lunch break, and I go for a short walk outside. When I finish work, I close my computer and put it in a drawer. I also call a colleague every day, just to chat.
Now I enjoy both. At home, I can concentrate better. At the office, I can see my friends and share ideas.

title: The Music Festival
paragraphs: Last summer, I went to a big music festival with three friends. It lasted for four days, and more than fifty thousand people came. There were five stages and more than a hundred bands.

We camped in a big field with thousands of other people. Our tent was small, and the ground was hard. On the second night, it rained a lot, and everything got wet and muddy. My new white shoes were brown at the end of the festival.

But the music was fantastic. We saw our favorite band on the main stage on Saturday night. They played for two hours, and everybody sang along. We also discovered some new bands that we didn't know before. Between concerts, we ate food from different countries and danced.
When I got home, I was very tired and very dirty. I slept for fourteen hours. But it was one of the best weeks of my life. Next year, I am definitely going again.

title: Traditions for Lost Teeth
paragraphs: When children lose their first teeth, many families have special traditions. These traditions are different in different countries, and some of them are quite strange.

In the United States, children put their tooth under their pillow at night. They believe that the tooth fairy comes while they are asleep. She takes the tooth and leaves some money. In many Spanish-speaking countries, it isn't a fairy, but a little mouse who takes the tooth.

In some countries in Asia, children throw their teeth. If it is a tooth from the top of the mouth, they throw it down to the ground. If it is from the bottom, they throw it up onto the roof. People believe this helps the new tooth grow straight and strong.
In other places, children give their teeth to an animal, or their parents keep them in a small box. All these traditions help children feel brave and happy about something that can be a little scary.

title: My Life as a Chef
paragraphs: I have worked as a chef for fifteen years. Now I have my own small restaurant, but I started in a big hotel kitchen when I was eighteen. My first job was washing vegetables and cleaning the floors.

Life in a kitchen is hard. You work long hours, often twelve hours a day. You work in the evenings, on the weekends, and on holidays, when other people are relaxing. The kitchen is hot and noisy, and everybody is in a hurry. Sometimes the head chef shouted at me, and I wanted to quit.

But I loved cooking, so I stayed. I watched the other chefs and learned from them. After a few years, I became a chef myself. Then I worked in restaurants in three different countries. I learned a lot about different kinds of food.
Today, my restaurant is small, with only twelve tables. I cook food from my grandmother's village. When people enjoy my food, I feel that all the hard work was worth it.

title: The Town That Sleeps
paragraphs: In some countries in southern Europe, many small towns have a tradition called the siesta. In the afternoon, from about two o'clock to five o'clock, shops close and the streets are empty. People go home to eat lunch and rest.

The siesta started a long time ago, because the afternoons in summer are very hot. It was too hot to work outside in the fields. So people worked early in the morning and again in the evening, when it was cooler.

For tourists, the siesta can be a surprise. Last summer, I visited a small town in Spain. At three o'clock, I wanted to buy some water, but every shop was closed. The town was so quiet that I could hear the birds. In the evening, everything opened again, and the streets were full of families until midnight.
Today, many people in big cities don't take a siesta anymore. But in small towns, the tradition is still alive.

title: My Pen Pal
paragraphs: When I was twelve, my English teacher gave every student in our class a pen pal. Mine was a girl called Akiko from Osaka, in Japan. We wrote letters to each other in English, because it was the only language we both knew.

In her first letter, Akiko told me about her family, her school, and her favorite food. She sent me a photo of her cat and a small origami bird. I wrote back about my town, my brother, and my love of soccer. Every letter took about two weeks to arrive, and I always ran to the mailbox after school.
We wrote to each other for six years. Our English got better and better. We told each other about our problems, our dreams, and our first loves.
Last year, I finally visited Japan. Akiko met me at the airport, and we recognized each other immediately. We cried and laughed at the same time. After twenty years, we are still friends.

title: The Forgotten Umbrella
paragraphs: Every morning, Mr. Hall took the same train to work. He always sat in the same seat, next to the window, and read the newspaper. One rainy Monday, he left his black umbrella on the train.

The next morning, he saw a young woman with his umbrella. She was sitting in his seat. "Excuse me," he said, "I think that is my umbrella." The woman smiled. "I know," she said. "I found it yesterday. I wanted to give it back to you." She knew he took this train every day.

They started talking. Her name was Jane, and she worked in the library near his office. The next day, they sat together again. And the next day. Soon, they were talking all the way to the city every morning.
A year later, Mr. Hall and Jane got married. At the wedding, Mr. Hall gave a short speech. He held up the black umbrella and said, "This is the best thing I ever lost."

title: Plastic in the Ocean
paragraphs: Every year, millions of tons of plastic go into the oceans. It comes from rivers, beaches, and ships. Plastic bags, bottles, and food packages float on the water for many years, because plastic doesn't disappear easily. Some plastic stays in the sea for hundreds of years.

This is a big problem for sea animals. Turtles often eat plastic bags, because they look like jellyfish. Birds eat small pieces of plastic and feed them to their babies. Fish and whales can get stuck in old fishing nets. Many animals die every year because of plastic.
Plastic is also a problem for people. Very small pieces of plastic are now in fish, salt, and even drinking water. Scientists are still studying how this affects our health.

But we can all help. We can use fewer plastic bags and bottles. We can bring our own bags to the supermarket and carry a metal water bottle. And we can recycle more. Small changes, by millions of people, can make a big difference.

title: Summer on the Farm
paragraphs: When I was a child, I spent every summer at my grandparents' farm. It was far from the city, in a green valley with a river. My parents worked, so I stayed there for six weeks every year.

Life on the farm was very different from my life at home. There was no television, and we went to bed early. In the morning, I woke up to the sound of the rooster. I helped my grandmother collect eggs from the chickens and my grandfather feed the cows. In the afternoon, I swam in the river with the children from the next farm.

My grandmother was a wonderful cook. Everything came from the farm: the vegetables, the milk, the eggs, and the fruit. In August, we made jam from the strawberries and plums. The whole kitchen smelled sweet.
Now my grandparents are gone, and another family lives on the farm. But I often think about those summers. They were the happiest days of my childhood.

title: The Wrong Address
paragraphs: It was late at night, and Paula was tired. She got into a taxi at the airport and gave the driver her address: "Twelve Green Street, please." The driver nodded, and they left.

After forty minutes, the taxi stopped. Paula looked out of the window. It was a small house in a street she didn't know. "This isn't my street," she said. The driver looked at his phone. "Twelve Green Road," he said. "You said Green Road." Paula laughed. "No, Green Street! It's on the other side of the city."
The driver was very embarrassed. He apologized many times. Then he turned off the meter. "I will take you home for free," he said. "It was my mistake."

On the long drive, they started talking. He told her about his family and his country. She told him about her trip. When they arrived, it was two o'clock in the morning. Paula gave him a big tip anyway. "Thank you for the interesting conversation," she said.

title: The Giant Panda
paragraphs: The giant panda is one of the most famous animals in the world. It is big, black and white, and it looks very friendly. Pandas live in the mountains of central China, in cool, wet forests.

Pandas eat almost only bamboo. An adult panda eats between twelve and thirty-eight kilos of bamboo every day. It spends about fourteen hours a day eating. Bamboo doesn't have much energy, so pandas move slowly and sleep a lot.
Baby pandas are very small when they are born. They weigh only about one hundred grams, and they are pink and have almost no fur. They stay with their mothers for about two years.

Some years ago, pandas were in danger. There were very few left, because people cut down their forests. But China created special parks to protect them, and now there are more pandas than before. They are still rare, but their future looks better.

title: The Big Exam
paragraphs: Last June, I had a very important English exam. I needed a good grade for my university application. I studied for six months. Every evening after work, I studied grammar and vocabulary for two hours.
The night before the exam, I couldn't sleep. I kept thinking about all the things I didn't know. In the morning, I couldn't eat breakfast. I arrived at the exam center an hour early.

The exam had four parts: reading, writing, listening, and speaking. The reading was OK, and the writing was not too bad. But the listening was very difficult. The people spoke very fast, and I missed some answers. I felt terrible during the lunch break.

In the afternoon, I had the speaking test. The examiner was very friendly, and I started to relax. We talked about travel and my job. I made some mistakes, but I spoke a lot. Six weeks later, I got the results. I passed with a good grade. I was so happy that I cried.

title: Fixing My Bike
paragraphs: Last weekend, my bike had a flat tire. Usually, I take it to the bike shop, but this time, I decided to fix it myself. I watched a video on the internet and bought a repair kit.

First, I turned the bike upside down. Then I took the wheel off. That was the easy part. Next, I had to take the tire off the wheel. It was very tight, and it took me twenty minutes. My hands were black and dirty. Then I found the hole in the inner tube. It was very small. A piece of glass made it.
I put a small patch on the hole and waited for the glue to dry. Then I put everything back together. That was harder than taking it off. Finally, I pumped up the tire.
I was very proud. The repair took two hours, and the bike shop does it in ten minutes. But I learned something new, and next time, it will be faster.

title: A Long Bus Trip
paragraphs: Last year, I traveled across South America by bus for two months. Buses are the cheapest way to travel there, and they go almost everywhere. Some trips were short, but some were more than twenty hours long.

The long-distance buses were surprisingly comfortable. The seats went back almost like a bed, and some buses served dinner. I usually traveled at night, so I didn't have to pay for a hotel. But it was not always easy to sleep, because the roads in the mountains had many curves.

From the window, I saw amazing places: high mountains with snow, green jungles, and dry deserts. I met many interesting people on the buses. An old man shared his fruit with me and told me about his village. A family taught me some words in their language.
Traveling by bus is slow, but you see the real country. I learned more on those buses than in any guidebook.

title: The Bird on the Balcony
paragraphs: Last spring, a small bird made a nest on my balcony. It was in an old flower pot in the corner. At first, I didn't notice it. Then one morning, I heard a lot of noise and saw the bird carrying small pieces of grass.

I decided not to use the balcony for a few weeks. I didn't want to scare the bird. Every morning, I watched her through the window while I drank my coffee. After about two weeks, there were four small blue eggs in the nest.

Two weeks later, the eggs opened. Four tiny babies with no feathers were in the nest. They were always hungry. The mother and father bird flew back and forth all day with insects and worms. The babies opened their mouths wide and made a lot of noise.
After three more weeks, the babies were big enough to fly. One morning, the nest was empty. I was a little sad, but the next spring, the birds came back.

title: A Phone in the Taxi
paragraphs: Last month, I left my phone in a taxi. I only noticed when I got home and wanted to call my sister. My whole life was on that phone: my photos, my contacts, my work emails, and my bank app. I felt sick.

I used my laptop to find my phone with a special app. It showed a small dot on a map. The phone was moving around the city. I called my number from my laptop, but nobody answered. I was sure that somebody had stolen it.
Then, about an hour later, my laptop rang. It was the taxi driver. He found my phone on the back seat and saw my call. "Where do you live?" he asked. "I can bring it to you after my work."
At midnight, he knocked on my door with my phone. I wanted to give him some money, but he said no. "Just do the same for somebody else one day," he said. I will never forget his kindness.

title: The Sandwich Shop
paragraphs: On the corner of my street, there is a tiny sandwich shop. It has only three tables, and there is always a line at lunchtime. The owner is a big, friendly man called Sal. He has worked there for thirty years.

Sal makes every sandwich by hand. He bakes his own bread every morning at five o'clock. He uses fresh vegetables from a farm outside the city and cheese from a small dairy. His most famous sandwich has roast chicken, cheese, tomatoes, and a special green sauce. Nobody knows the recipe for the sauce.
The sandwiches are not cheap, but they are huge. One sandwich is enough for lunch and dinner. Many office workers come from far away just to eat there.

Last year, a big company wanted to buy Sal's shop and open more shops in other cities. They offered him a lot of money, but he said no. "I don't want more money," he said. "I want to make good sandwiches for my neighbors."

title: Learning to Swim at Forty
paragraphs: I never learned to swim as a child. My family lived far from the sea, and there was no swimming pool in our town. When I went on vacation with friends, I always stayed on the beach while they swam. I felt embarrassed.

Last year, when I turned forty, I decided it was time to learn. I found a class for adults at the pool near my office. There were five other students, and most of them were older than me. That made me feel better.

The first lesson was terrible. I was scared to put my face in the water, and I held on to the side of the pool. Our teacher, Ben, was very patient. He said, "Don't fight the water. Relax, and it will hold you." Slowly, I began to trust the water.
After three months, I could swim twenty-five meters without stopping. Last summer, I swam in the sea for the first time. I was so happy that I laughed and swallowed salty water.

title: The Night of the Fire
